<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 3 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Topological Manifolds</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">3.1</span> Topological Spaces</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>The <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">powerset</span> <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{M})\)</span> of a set <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> is the set of all possible subsets of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>The set <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}\subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{M})\)</span> defines a <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">topology</span> on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, denoted as <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\)</span>, if and only if:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p>The topology contains the empty set and the whole space itself: <span class="math inline">\(\emptyset \in \mathcal{O}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M} \in \mathcal{O}\)</span>,</p></li>
<li><p>The intersection of any two sets that belong to the topology, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{V}\in \mathcal{O}\)</span> (referred to as <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">open sets</span>), is also an open set: <span class="math inline">\(\forall \mathcal{U}, \mathcal{V} \in \mathcal{O} \rightarrow \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V} \in \mathcal{O}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>Any union of open sets (even an infinite one) is also an open set: <span class="math inline">\(\bigcup_{\alpha}\mathcal{U}_{\alpha}\in \mathcal{O}\)</span>, where <span class="math inline">\(\alpha\)</span> denotes an arbitrary index set.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>A set <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{M}\)</span> is said to be <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">closed</span> under the topology <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\)</span> if its complement is open: <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{C} \text{ is closed} \iff \mathcal{M} \setminus \mathcal{C} \in \mathcal{O}\)</span>. Note that a set can be open, closed, both (clopen), or neither, depending on the topology.</p></li>
<li><p>The doublet <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{M}\right)\)</span> is a <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">topological space</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>Given a topological space <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\right)\)</span>, the <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">inherited topology</span> (or subspace topology) on a subset <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{N} \subseteq \mathcal{M}\)</span> is defined as  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \left.\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}}\right|_{\mathcal{M}} \coloneqq
            \left\lbrace \mathcal{N} \cap \mathcal{U} : \mathcal{U} \in \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}} \right\rbrace.
        \end{align*}</span>  That is, a subset <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathcal{N}\)</span> is declared open in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{N}\)</span> if and only if it can be written as the intersection of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{N}\)</span> with an open set <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span> from the ambient topology <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>The <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span> <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">standard topology</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{R}^d}\)</span>, is  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{R}^d} \coloneqq
            \Big\{\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \;\Big|\;
            \forall p \in \mathcal{U}\;\exists r&gt;0:\; B_r(p) \subseteq \mathcal{U}\Big\},
        \end{align*}</span>  where the soft/open ball of radius <span class="math inline">\(r\)</span> about <span class="math inline">\(p=(p_1,\dots,p_d)\)</span> is  <span class="math display">\[
            B_r(p) \coloneqq \Big\{ q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)\in\mathbb{R}^d \;\Big|\; \sum_{i=1}^d (q_i-p_i)^2 &lt; r^2\Big\}.
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p>A topological space <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\right)\)</span> is <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">Hausdorff</span> if any two distinct points can be separated by disjoint open sets:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \forall \, p, q \in \mathcal{M}, \; p \neq q, \;\; \exists \, \mathcal{U}, \mathcal{V} \in \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}} :
            \; p \in \mathcal{U}, \; q \in \mathcal{V}, \; \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V} = \emptyset.
        \end{align*}</span>  For instance, <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{R}^d}\right)\)</span> is Hausdorff: take two open balls centred at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(q\)</span>, of radius half their distance.</p></li>
<li><p>The map <span class="math inline">\(\phi: \mathcal{M} \rightarrow \mathcal{N}\)</span> is <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">continuous</span> w.r.t. <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\right)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{N}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}}\right)\)</span> if and only if the <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">preimage</span> of every open set in the target space <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{N}\)</span> is also an open set in the domain <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, i.e.  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \forall \mathcal{V} \in \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}} \rightarrow
            \mathrm{preim}_{\phi}(\mathcal{V}) \coloneqq \left\lbrace p \in \mathcal{M} \mid
            \phi(p) \in \mathcal{V}\right\rbrace \in \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}.
        \end{align*}</span>  This encodes the idea that <span class="math inline">\(\phi\)</span> does not “tear” or “break” the underlying topological structure.</p></li>
<li><p>Given two topological spaces <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}} \right)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{N}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}} \right)\)</span>, a map <span class="math inline">\(\phi \colon \mathcal{M} \longrightarrow \mathcal{N}\)</span>, is a <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">homeomorphism</span> w.r.t. <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}} \right)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{N}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}} \right)\)</span> – if and only if:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><span class="math inline">\(\phi\)</span> is bijective, hence invertible, i.e. there exists an inverse map: <span class="math inline">\(\phi^{-1} \colon \mathcal{N} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><span class="math inline">\(\phi\)</span> is continuous w.r.t. <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\right)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{N}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}} \right)\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><span class="math inline">\(\phi^{-1}\)</span> is also continuous w.r.t. <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{N}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{N}} \right)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\left( \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\right)\)</span>.</p></li>
</ol></li>
<li><p>A topological space <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\right)\)</span> is <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">second countable</span> if its topology admits a countable <span class="dg-term dg-term-blue">basis</span>, i.e. a countable collection <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{M}}\)</span> such that every open set is a union of elements of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{B}\)</span>. For instance, the open balls with rational centres and rational radii form a countable basis of <span class="math inline">\(\left(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{R}^d}\right)\)</span>.</p></li>
</ul>
